Trendline breaks (context only)
  • Timeframes: weekly, daily, 65m, 15m. Each column shows one compact chip: the highest-scoring latest break across the short (“s”) and broad (“b”) lines. Lines join the two latest causally confirmed swing highs (descending resistance, ↑) or lows (rising support, ↓).
  • Chip labels: Break (close just confirmed), Hold (still beyond the line), Retest (retested and closed beyond), Failed (failed to hold), or “—” if there is no close-confirmed break. n/a = data unavailable or history too short. The number is the 0–100 quality score. Color follows direction (green ↑ / red ↓) and strength (strong ≥75, moderate 50–74, weak <50). A left edge mark highlights a fresh Break. ≠ means the other horizon differs in direction or state — hover for that line, click the chip for full short/broad detail.
  • A break needs a completed-bar close beyond the line by 0.25×ATR14. Partial periods are excluded; 65m and 15m bars are built from 5m regular-session data anchored at the 9:30 ET open.
  • Quality score: touches (max 40) + time held, per-timeframe tiers (max 35) + break volume (max 25); failed to hold = 0. “Active break on” filters to Break or Retest on the selected timeframe(s).
  • Not part of the score, gate or sort. A break is not proof a trend has reversed.
How the score works (v2, 0–100)
  • 1. Gate (pass/fail, not points): nearest-expiry ATM contract needs a two-sided quote (bid >0, ask ≥ bid), spread ≤15% of mid, open interest ≥100, a valid IV, ≥260 daily bars of history, and quotes captured at/after 9:45 ET. Failing names show “Gated out” with the reason and no score.
  • 2. Event list: names with earnings before the nearest expiry go to a separate list and are ranked only among themselves.
  • 3. Score: each input is turned into a percentile rank (0–1) among today’s gated names, then weighted: vol cheapness 30 = ln(1-year realized vol ÷ ATM IV), higher ranks higher; IV term slope 15 = ~1-year ATM IV − nearest ATM IV; direction 25 = ½ rank of a 1-month pullback (reversal) + ¼ rank of 12-month momentum skipping the last month + ¼ rank of closeness to the 52-week high; low idiosyncratic vol 10 = residual volatility vs SPY over 63 days, lower ranks higher; cost 10 = bid/ask spread ÷ expected move to expiry, lower ranks higher.
  • Renormalised: the call−put IV spread (10) is left out until IV is recomputed from mid prices; its weight is spread across the other components (so the five shown sum to 100). Any input missing for a row is also dropped and listed for that row.
  • Display only: support/resistance, IV rank, pullback %, analyst consensus/targets and trendlines are context; they are not in the score, gate or sort. The legacy fit score and pass flags are still computed and shown as “Legacy fit”.
Prices are prior completed sessions only (today’s bar excluded). Δ≈0.45 strike uses Black-Scholes delta from the chain IV. Implied move = ATM IV × √(days/365). ⚑E = earnings before that expiry. Numbers only — the score measures fit to these criteria, not future returns.

Weekly puts Candidates matching your criteria — not a recommendation. Score v2: gate first, then daily percentile ranks across today's gated put names. Same expiry rule as calls (nearest ≥7 days out).

How the put score works (v2, 0–100)
  • Gate: same as calls, applied to the nearest-expiry ATM put (two-sided quote, spread ≤15% of mid, OI ≥100, valid IV, ≥260 daily bars, quotes at/after 9:45 ET). Earnings before expiry → separate event list.
  • Score: vol cheapness 30 = ln(1-year realized vol ÷ ATM put IV); IV term slope 15 = ~1-year ATM call IV − nearest ATM call IV; direction 25 = mirror of calls (½ rank of the 1-month gain, ¼ rank of weak 12-month momentum, ¼ rank of distance below the 52-week high); low idiosyncratic vol 10; cost 10 = put spread ÷ expected move. Call−put IV spread (10) left out and renormalised, as on Calls.
  • Display only: resistance, overextension, IV rank, analyst info and trendlines. Legacy put fit score and pass flags shown as “Legacy fit”.
